You also want to try to expand aggressively using Sweden's military bonuses and be willing to settle Cities without Fresh Water and in Tundra that other civs might not prioritize so that you can build as many of the Bastu as possible.
uniqueBuildings.flavor: The Swedish Bad Stuga (bath cabin), or Bastu, is a small cabin designed as a bathing and dry heat spa. A stove or furnace heats the room to 200°F before patrons enter, where they will recline and sweat. Bastus are a social affair, places for discussion and relaxation with family and friends, but were also places for food curing and childbirth in earlier times. It is not known where or when Scandinavian sweat baths were first created, but it was well before the Christianization of Scandinavia, as evidenced by their ubiquity throughout medieval Europe. By the time written accounts first described Scandinavian sweat baths, Nordic countries had already created varied and distinct cultures surrounding them. The health benefits of heat baths are many and varied. Sessions have been shown to relieve cold symptoms and increase pain thresholds. They also help with rheumatic pain and fatigue, and may even reduce the risk of dementia. Prolonged use of a sauna has been linked to reduced male fertility, however, and heat baths should never be enjoyed while under the effects of alcohol.

uniqueAbility.name: Serenissima
uniqueAbility.description: Cannot create Settlers or annex Cities. Trade Route cap doubled, target restrictions removed. Free at . Puppet provide 50% yields and supply (other civs: 30%) and can make Gold purchases and gain Happiness like normal Cities.

uniqueUnits.name: Merchant of Venice
uniqueUnits.strategy: The is the Venetian unique unit, replacing the . It generates more when performing a trade mission. It can acquire a City-State outright, bringing it under Venetian control as a puppet. It can also found a Colonia, which is a city that starts puppeted with 3 Citizens, claims 3 additional tiles, and immediately receives a and a . The is expended when used in any of these ways. Note: the bonuses for constructing buildings from the Progress and Industry policy branches do not apply to the buildings automatically constructed on founding!

uniqueUnits.name: Great Galleass
uniqueUnits.strategy: The Great Galleass performs similarly to the Galleass, but is more resilient in battle and has a stronger ranged attack. Starts with the Bombardment I Promotion.

uniqueUnits.name: Fusta
uniqueUnits.strategy: Fusta are to Venice as the Galleass is to other Civilizations, and Venetian Liburna upgrade to the Fusta rather than the Great Galleass. The Fusta is not really a direct replacement, having a slightly weaker ranged strength is compensated by a lower cost and additional movement point. However its truly unique feature is costing no military supply, meaning you can pump out an enormous fleet of Fusta to swarm your opponents, protect your larger and slower ships, and extend your naval presence to every corner of the world's oceans.
uniqueUnits.flavor: Fusta, or galliots, were small galleys with no more than 35 sailors. Exceptionally light and fast, the Venetians originally used them to maintain a standing navy against pirates, but the ship quickly became a favorite of the pirates themselves. The shallow draft, maneuverability and speed of the Fusta made them a legend throughout the Mediterranean.

uniqueBuildings.name: Piazza San Marco
uniqueBuildings.strategy: Unique Venetian replacement for the . In addition to the bonuses of the , provides additional Food, Production, Gold, Science, City Security, and Military Supply, and an extra boost to the city's Great People generation. This building also reduces the cooldown of purchasing civilian units and removes the cooldown of purchasing military units. Unlocks the ability for Venice to build 1 of 3 unique buildings once Guilds is researched. Unlike the , the is made available with the discovery of , does not require a in the city, but can only be built in the Capital.
uniqueBuildings.description: Unlocks access to Murano Glassworks, Arsenale di Venezia, and Rialto District once Guilds is researched.
uniqueBuildings.flavor: Piazza San Marco (often known in English as St Mark's Square), is the principal public square of Venice, Italy, where it is generally known just as "the Piazza" (la Piazza). All other urban spaces in the city (except the Piazzetta and the Piazzale Roma) are called "campi" (fields). The Piazzetta (the 'little Piazza') is an extension of the Piazza towards the lagoon in its south east corner (see plan). The two spaces together form the social, religious and political centre of Venice and are commonly considered together.

uniqueAbility.name: Iklwa
uniqueAbility.description: -50% Gold maintenance for Melee and Gunpowder Units. All Units require 25% less Experience for Promotions. Your military ignores Alliance and Protection penalties and is 50% more effective at intimidating City-States.

uniqueUnits.name: Impi
uniqueUnits.strategy: The is the Zulu unique unit, replacing the . Before engaging in an melee attack, it performs a spear throw attack that can damage or kill the enemy unit. This will weaken the defender before melee combat ensues, ensuring that it takes less damage when attacking compared to its contemporary units. It also has a Combat Strength bonus when fighting against Gunpowder units, making it a deadly unit well into the Industrial Era.

uniqueUnits.name: Induna
uniqueUnits.strategy: The InDuna's primary unique bonuses over a Great General are that when expended it provides experience to the unit it's stacked with and creates an Isibaya which places a Cattle Resource adjacent to it and adjacent Pastures receive Food, Production, and Culture. The Isibaya should still primarily be used for military purposes like a Citadel but where possible trying to build it within the working radius of a city and adjacent to Pastures should be considered so you get the economic bonuses. You should always make sure to have a military unit stacked with the InDuna when constructing an Isibaya and its usually best to try to give the bonus experience to higher level units especially ranged or siege units. This is due to these unit types being easier to keep alive longer compared to melee units and that they tend to gain experience slower so the bonus experience is more impactful.
uniqueUnits.flavor: An InDuna can widely be translated to any leader of men, in commerce, in politics, and in war. An InDuna guided each regiment, or 'ibutho', of young Zulu men and he in turn answered to senior izinDuna who controlled the corps. One or more of these elder chiefs might accompany a big force on an important mission, but there was no single "field marshal" in command of all Zulu forces. Regimental izinDuna, like the non-commissioned officers of today's army, were important for morale and discipline. This was demonstrated during the battle of Isandlwana, where the army led by Ntshingwayo kaMahole outmaneuvered and destroyed a British column. Ntshingwayo kaMahole and his fellow izinDuna snuck a Zulu force of 20,000 men behind the British, hiding them in a valley only 7 miles from the British camp. When discovered sitting in complete silence by scouts, the izinDuna spurred their men into action and closed the remaining distance with lightning speed.

uniqueBuildings.name: Iziko
uniqueBuildings.strategy: The Iziko's main unique bonus is that it provides culture when any of your units level up and scales with the number of cities you have it built in your empire. This synergizes well with the Zulu Unique Ability as less experience is needed for each unit level. To maximize the bonus, you should try to build instead of purchase military units so they start with full experience and have as many buildings and other bonuses that provide starting unit experience. You'll also generally want to play aggressively with Zulu so you can be actively gaining experience through combat to level up your existing units and expanding to have more cities to build the Iziko.
uniqueBuildings.description: Possible Theming Bonuses: +4 and for two Foreign Great Works of Writing. +4 and for two Domestic Great Works of Writing.
uniqueBuildings.flavor: An Iziko is a simple hearth used as a gathering place for Zulu communities. The fireplace was revered as a source for food, warmth, dreams, and ancestral ties. It is from these gatherings that a sense of community and identity was formed, and young Zulus could perform and bond. The fireplace is used metaphorically for the "cooking of songs" in isicathamiya stage performances, a modern offshoot of traditional Zulu music. Dreams were an essential part of communicating with ancestors and formed part of a deeply rooted Zulu religion. Some isicathamiya musicians claim some of their songs were created in the spiritual realm or given to them by their ancestors. "A person is a person because of other people" - Zulu proverb

uniqueImprovements.name: Isibaya
uniqueImprovements.description: Unique Zulu Great Person Tile Improvement, replacing the Citadel. Can only be constructed by a . Provides Production, Science, and Culture. Adjacent Pastures receive Food, Production, and Culture. Building an Isibaya claims adjacent tiles and places a Cattle Resource adjacent to it. Units standing on an Isibaya receive +100% Tile Defense. Deals 30 damage to adjacent Enemy Units.
uniqueImprovements.flavor: An Isibaya is a Zulu homestead and defensive structure. The Isibaya is laid out in a circular pattern with a cattle enclosure at the centre, ringed by huts, palisades, and mud walls. The layout and function are reminiscent of a European corral, hence the Afrikaans term for Amabaya, "Kraal". Cattle were central to the life and economy of the Zulu Kingdom. Cattle were a sign of status, wealth, and power, and were instrumental for feeding and arming the amabutho regiments of the Zulu army.
